title: Quantifying membrane protein oligomerization using two-dimensional fluorescence intensity fluctuation spectrometry
protocol: Generate cell lines stably expressing membrane receptors of interest.
Maintain a healthy cell culture on T-25 flask.
Allow cells to recover from deep freeze by performing at least two passages if revived from deep freeze.
Subculture cells if they are more than 85% confluent on the flask.
Lift cells from T-25 flask and plate them onto poly-d-lysine coated chambered cover glass.
Seed between 500-1000 cells/mm² of coverslip growth area.
Allow the cells to grow for 36-48 hours in a humidified incubator.
Aspirate cell growth medium before preparing for imaging.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
If exposing cells to ligand, add ligand solution to cells for desired time.
If no ligand is being used, simply add PBS to cells for the same amount of time.
Remove ligand solution or PBS and add 1.5 mL of 4% formaldehyde fixing solution.
Leave cells in fixing solution for 20 minutes.
Remove fixing solution.
Resuspend cells in PBS; cells now ready for imaging.
Set the pixel dwell time for the measuring system to be at least a factor of five times shorter than the two-dimensional characteristic diffusion time, τ<sub>D</sub>, of the receptor under study.
Obtain fluorescence images from several hundred cells for each type of experimental condition.

Search for cell/cells using scanning parameters with reduced power or much shorter exposure time compared to the settings used for actual data collection so as not to expose cells to too much laser light.
Focus on the basolateral membrane of a cell or group of cells using the preview scan.
Take fluorescence scan of the focused cell/cells.
Repeat steps i-iii until fluorescence images have been acquired from several hundred cells.
Obtain fluorescence images from cells expressing monomeric form of the fluorescent marker fused to receptor of interest.
Obtain fluorescence images from cells expressing tandem dimer form of the fluorescent marker fused to receptor of interest.
Apply the same imaging conditions used for cells with fluorescently labeled receptor of interest.
Obtain fluorescence images of sub-diffraction sized fluorescent microspheres.
Laser spot scan the surface of a mirror slide in the plane of focus of the microscope.
Remove filters from detection pathway to prevent laser light from striking the detector.
Acquire scans at various laser powers.
Use transmitted light illuminator during acquisition with integration time settings similar to fluorescence scans.
Acquire scans at different levels of transmitted light intensity.
Measure the mean intensity in multiple ~10,000 pixel subregions of acquisitions where there are no cells/fluorophores present and average the results from these regions.
Determine slope and intercept for a plot of variance vs intensity for constant light source measurements.
Measure both the variance as well as mean intensity from small subregions of scans taken of the constant light source.
Construct a scatter plot of the variance vs average intensity from all of the subregions measured.
Use FIF Spectrometry Suite to demarcate regions of interest (ROI) on fluorescence images of cells separately expressing monomeric and tandem dimer forms of the fluorescent marker.
Load 2D fluorescence images for a given sample.
Select ROIs using a polygon tool.
Draw the polygon such that it encompasses the majority of the region inside the cell boundary.
Segment each ROI into smaller segments using a maximum segment size of 500 pixels.
Use FIF Spectrometry Suite to calculate the effective brightness for each segment generated in the images of cells expressing monomeric and dimeric fluorescent protein constructs.
Input the values for average background intensity, S, and σ² determined in steps C1 and C2 above.
Determine the monomeric effective brightness value, εproto, from the distribution of monomer and dimer brightness values calculated in C4.
Simultaneously fit the two spectrograms with Gaussian functions.
Set the Gaussian peak position simulating the monomer distribution to be εproto.
Set the Gaussian peak position simulating the dimer peak position to be 2εproto.
Use the same standard deviation for both Gaussian functions, but allow it to vary as a fitting parameter.
Use the best fit value of εproto as the monomeric effective brightness value.
Use FIF Spectrometry Suite to extract brightness and concentration from each segment.
Calculate the brightness and concentration using mean and standard deviation from intensity histograms.
Create a two-dimensional surface plot for the frequency of occurrence of effective brightness-concentration pairs.
Generate brightness spectrograms for various concentration ranges.
Perform meta-analysis of brightness spectrograms using FIF Spectrometry Suite.
Obtain oligomer species fraction plots as a function of protomer concentration.
Fit the individual brightness spectrogram for a single concentration range with an array of Gaussian functions.
Calculate the area underneath each Gaussian, relative to the total area under the entire histogram.
Repeat the fitting process for all concentration ranges to determine the relative abundance values for each oligomer size.
